name: Can I build a room addition on a small lot in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Can I build a room addition on a small lot in Los Angeles, Glendale, or Pasadena?
mainEntity.text: Can I build a room addition on a small lot in Los Angeles, Glendale, or Pasadena?

acceptedAnswer.text: Small-lot additions are possible, but the design has to fit the site rather than forcing the site to fit the design. Setbacks, lot coverage, height limits, existing easements, and required open space can all reduce the amount of buildable area. In some cases, a second-story addition or a carefully designed bump-out may work better than expanding outward. Access for construction is another major factor, because tight side yards and limited staging space can increase labor time and cost. Homeowners should also consider daylight, ventilation, privacy, and how the addition will connect to the existing home. A good feasibility review early in the process can show what is realistic before spending money on full architectural plans. On small lots, smart design often matters more than raw square footage.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but small lots often make room additions harder because of setbacks, lot coverage limits, and access constraints. The project may still be possible if the design works within zoning rules and preserves required open space, light, and parking requirements.
